subject: Re: Packaging choices — seat gating, upgrade clauses & pilot credits
messages:
From: Nora Patel <nora@catalyst.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: eli.moreno@catalyst.ai
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging options + seat gating question

Hi Markus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We had a quick follow-up from procurement: as we consider a 12-month commitment, we want clarity on two things before we take this to execs:

1) Seat gating: our usage is bursty — we need the ability to temporarily add seats for specific teams without re-contracting. Can the Compact tier be configured to allow temporary seat add-ons that automatically expire
after 30 days? What does that look like on pricing/overage?

2) Upgrade path: if we commit to Compact now but need to move to Throughput tier in Q1, what are the proration mechanics and can you preserve pilot credits/discounts we agree to?

Also looping in Eli from procurement who will own contract language.

Could you send a short options matrix and a sample clause for seat gating/upgrades?

Appreciate it —
Nora
Nora Patel
Head of Strategic Accounts, Catalyst Health
Phone: (415) 555-0198

Attachment: Catalyst_RFP_Summary.pdf (ref)

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Nora Patel <nora@catalyst.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, eli.moreno@catalyst.ai
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging options + seat gating question

Nora —

Thanks for the clear asks. Short answer: yes, we can support temporary seat gating and a smooth upgrade path. Below is a concise matrix and the sample clause we typically propose. I'll attach a one-page MAP and term-sheet draft for procurement.

Options matrix (high level):
- Compact + Seat Gating (recommended pilot): base includes 50 seats, optional temporary seats in 10-seat increments, auto-expire at 30 days. Temporary seats billed at Compact per-seat rate + 15% surge fee. Temporary seats do not consume reserved throughput capacity.
- Throughput tier (stable production): reserved capacity, seats uncapped; migration preserves usage history for billing reconciliation.

Upgrade/proration basics:
- If you upgrade mid-term we prorate remaining committed fees to the new tier; pilot credits applied against outstanding invoices first. Example: upgrade on day 120 of 365 -> remaining 245 days credited pro-rata to new tier.
- We can include a one-time credit equal to up to 25% of pilot fees if upgrade to Throughput is signed within first 6 months.

Sample seat-gating clause (draft):
"""
Customer may request temporary seat allocations ("Temporary Seats") in 10-seat increments for periods not to exceed thirty (30) consecutive days. Temporary Seats are billed at the then-current Compact temporary seat rate plus a transient surcharge of fifteen percent (15%). Temporary Seats will automatically expire at the end of the requested period unless Customer requests an extension in writing and Supplier agrees. Temporary Seats do not reduce Customer's reserved throughput entitlement under any tier.
"""

Next steps: I will send the MAP and term sheet as attachments. Lauren — can you confirm if finance is comfortable with the 15% transient surcharge and the 25% pilot-to-upgrade credit cap for an initial 12-month contract? Aditya — can you provide the SKU/pricing lines I should put in the term sheet?

Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
Mobile: (650) 555-0112

Attachments: MAP_Catalyst_2026Q3.xlsx, Catalyst_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, Nora Patel <nora@catalyst.ai>, eli.moreno@catalyst.ai
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging options + seat gating question

Markus / Nora —

Quick internal note from finance: the 15% transient surcharge is acceptable for temporary seats if we limit the number of concurrent Temporary Seat pools to 3 per account without an uplift approval. For a 12-month term we can apply the pilot credit flow described but need the following in the term sheet:

- Clear definition of pilot credits (one-time amount, non-recurring) and that credits apply to invoice balance only (no cash refunds).
- Upgrade credit cap (25%) must be tied to signing timeframe (within first 6 months).
- Proration example included (we'll add a worked example table).

Nora — if Catalyst wants an exception to the 3 concurrent pools rule, we can discuss in exchange for a modest uplift or a longer committed term.

I'll review the term sheet PDF and push any line-item changes.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Director, Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Finance_QA_Notes.txt (internal)

From: Eli Moreno <eli.moreno@catalyst.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: Nora Patel <nora@catalyst.ai>, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging options + seat gating question

Markus / Lauren —

Appreciate the rapid follow-up and the draft clause. Procurement reviewed the MAP and term sheet. Two minor asks before we route to legal: 

1) Can the transient surcharge be capped per quarter (e.g., no more than $15k in transient surcharge fees per fiscal quarter) for our first year? This helps avoid bill shock.
2) For the upgrade credit: can you confirm the credit will be applied to the new tier's recurring fees (not only one-off setup/invoice items)? We need that spelled out in the clause.

If you can mark up the PDF and return, we'll aim to review with legal next week. We'd like to lock in a commercial term sheet this month.

Best —
Eli Moreno
Sourcing Manager, Catalyst Health
Phone: (617) 555-0224
